newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Bearish double-top seen in dollar/yen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bearish double-top seen in dollar/yen.

text.p: The dollar's failure to push through the 117.35/45 yen threshold for a second consecutive session points to a bearish double-top formation in the rate, chartists said on Thursday.
Barring a near-term hurdle of the 117 level, technicians foresee additional weakness in dollar/yen, and peg the 115.75/80 level as a key gauge of near-term support.
"Early this morning we went back almost to 117.40 and that gave us a double top," said Martin Autotte, technical foreign exchange analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp.
"And the fact that we're holding below 116.60 opens the downside for a move down to 115.80 initially and a possible extension down to 115.20," he added.
With a close below the 115.80 level, Autotte said a corrective drop in dollar/yen could evolve into a more major reversal in trend.
Scott Siller, senior technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch, concurred on dollar/yen's downside potential, noting bearish divergence on his daily studies.
"It looks like the highs near 117.50 are unconfirmed," Siller said.
"There's trendline support down at 115.75 and if we can take that out it could mean corrective weakness," he added.

Siller saw near-term downside potential to 114.65, which represents a 50 percent retracement of dollar/yen's climb since December 6. He said a move back above 117 was necessary to improve the upward bias in the rate.
Both Autotte and Siller noted a 7-1/2 year bearish trend line dating from June 1989 was keeping dollar/mark in check.
Autotte pegged it at 1.5960 while Siller saw it coming in just above the 1.60-even level.

"The fact that we haven't been able to close above that trendline gives me a bearish bias on dollar/mark," said Autotte. "I think we'll move below 1.58 in the days ahead," he added, putting initial support at 1.5855/60.
Siller was less negative on dollar/mark, noting an absence of strong bearish divergences that would indicate a correction in the rate.
"While there is a risk we pull back from this area on profit-taking and speculative shorts there are no real indicators (suggesting) we're headed lower," he said.
